result.summary: Headings that come from the output of a macro are no longer given section edit links and no longer count as page sections. Only macros that declare `:sections => true` (now `collapse`) keep their headings as sections. The included headings are still rendered normally, including anchors and TOC entries. Verified with the full non-system test suite (6079 runs, 0 failures) and rubocop (no offenses). Nothing was committed or pushed.

changes.summary: `macro` accepts a new `:sections` option (added to assert_valid_keys) and documents it. `collapse` is declared with `:sections => true`. Added `macro_with_sections?(name)` helper in Definitions.

inject_macros marks the headings of output from macros without `:sections` with a `data-non-section` attribute (via new `mark_non_section_headings`). parse_sections skips such headings: no edit link and no section number. parse_headings strips the marker so it does not appear in the final HTML. The HTML_RE/heading anchor behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

Added 4 tests: local headings around an include get edit links with section numbers matching the source; an include inside collapse keeps collapse's headings as sections; a macro declared with `:sections => true` keeps its heading as a section; a macro without the option does not.

acceptance.criterion: On a page with local headings and an included page, only the local headings get edit links, and their section numbers match the numbers used when editing the page
acceptance.evidence: New test test_section_edit_links_should_ignore_headings_of_included_page passes: Child page 1 from the include has no edit link, and Local B/Local C get section=2 and section=3, matching the raw source numbering. Against the original helper code this test fails.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests
acceptance.evidence: Four new tests in test/helpers/application_helper_test.rb (include, include inside collapse, :sections declared macro, undeclared macro). Run against original app/helpers/application_helper.rb, 3 of them fail (include, include in collapse, undeclared macro), confirming they detect the bug. The existing collapse section tests still pass.

acceptance.criterion: The existing test suite still passes
acceptance.evidence: `bin/rails test` (Ruby 4.0.0 from /opt/homebrew/opt/ruby@4, the system Ruby 2.6 is too old for Rails 8.1): 6079 runs, 31805 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 37 skips (pre-existing skips). Rubocop: 3 files inspected, no offenses.

harness_used: Read/Grep/Glob tools to locate the macro, heading and section code and the existing section tests
Bash to run rails tests with the Ruby 4 toolchain and rubocop
Existing test suite (bin/rails test) as regression check

harness_gaps.problem: The imported RTK.md does not exist in the repository, so that instruction could not be applied. Nothing in the repo referred to it.

No documented way to run the tests. The default system Ruby (2.6) is too old for Rails 8.1 and bundler 4.0.6 is required by Gemfile.lock. Working setup needed /opt/homebrew/opt/ruby@4/bin on PATH, and config/database.yml (sqlite) was already present.

The marker attribute is stripped only where parse_headings runs. Top-level calls with headings: false (the PDF export in wiki_pdf_helper.rb) keep the data-non-section attribute in their HTML output when a page uses include. This is harmless for the PDF renderer, but I did not verify the PDF output.
